title: Control evidence journal — SOC2 prep notes
content:
Top-level goal: prepare a minimal, reproducible evidence set for the first SOC2 readiness review. This is a working, messy notebook — capture ideas, queries, and quick commands to fetch artifacts.

High-level scope (what to show):
- Logical access: user & service account provisioning, MFA enforcement, privileged roles, SSO mappings.
- Change control: code review policy, merge gating, deployment approvals, release audit trail.
- Logging & monitoring: retention, access to logs, alerting playbooks, runbook attachments.
- Key management & secrets: KMS usage, rotation cadence, limited key access.
- Incident response: ticket trail, postmortem artifacts, customer notifications (if applicable).

Working checklist (evidence pockets):
- IAM: list of admin groups (exported CSV), sample user onboarding ticket, SSO assertion logs for 2 users.
- Service accounts: terraform state snippet + last credential rotation PR.
- PR/CR: Github PR with approvals + CI passing for 2 representative repos.
- Deploys: deployment timeline from CI system (timestamped), deployment runbook used.
- Logs: central logging query results showing retention >= 90 days, sample alert firing and incident ticket link.
- Backups: snapshot manifest + S3 lifecycle policy screenshots or JSON.
- Encryption: KMS policy JSON + example access logs.

Evidence naming convention (quick): 
redwood-evidence/<control-id>/<artifact-type>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<short-desc>.<ext>
Examples: redwood-evidence/AC-1/pr-archive/2026-02-10-ssr-pr-432.patch, redwood-evidence/LOG-2/log-export/2026-02-20-alert-sample.json

Quick queries & commands (save these) — adapt as needed:
- List admins (gcloud IAM): gcloud projects get-iam-policy $PROJECT --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.role | contains("roles/owner") or contains("roles/editor") or contains("roles/iam.admin"))'
- Get SSO assertions (Okta): export last 30d auth events CSV from Okta admin -> Reports -> System Log (filter: User Login)
- Fetch cloudtrail events for key usage (AWS): aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2026-01-01 --end-time 2026-03-01 --output json > cloudtrail-decrypt-sample.json
- ElasticSearch/Logging query (example): timestamp:[2026-01-01 TO 2026-03-01] AND severity:ERROR AND service:auth

Short scripts to automate harvest (notes):
- harvest_evidence.sh: iterate controls.csv -> run queries above -> zip artifacts into per-control folders -> upload to private S3 bucket (with bucket encryption). Keep minimal metadata file (control_id, query_cmd, last_collected_by, collection_date).
- Important: mark PII or redactions step; redact before attaching publicly shareable bits.

Control mapping (brain dump) — map to concrete artifacts:
- AC-1 (Access provisioning): IAM CSV export, onboarding ticket x2, onboarding checklist template (doc).
- AC-3 (MFA): IdP policy screenshot, exception list, enforcement rollout email.
- CC-4 (Change control): Github branch protection config, sample PR, CI pipeline run log.
- LOG-2 (Logging retention): storage lifecycle policy JSON, sample query + export, SLI graph for log ingestion volume.
- CR-1 (CR and incident): incident ticket + postmortem (redacted), alert -> pager duty incident timeline.

Open questions / blockers (to resolve quickly):
- Which SSO events are considered "evidence" by the auditor? Full system log export or filtered extracts? (Ask: audit scope owner)
- Do we need screenshots of console policies or JSON exports only?
- For on-prem/private deployments, what access logs are required from customer-managed infra? (Need legal to confirm)
- Retention mismatch: some log indexes TTL = 75 days. Need plan to extend to 90 days or provide export policy demonstrating cold storage.

Prioritization for next 2 weeks:
1) IAM admin list + 2 onboarding tickets (due in 3 days)
2) Harvest 90-day log sample + retention policy artifact (due in 7 days)
3) KMS policy export + proof of rotation (due in 10 days)
4) One representative PR + deploy audit trail (due in 14 days)

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep artifacts minimal: fewer, higher-quality artifacts beat many tiny noisy files. Auditors often prefer machine-readable exports (JSON/CSV) over screenshots but ask them.
- Prefer immutable exports with checksums (sha256) and record of who pulled them.
- For any redaction, preserve original and redacted with manifest explaining redaction reason.

Candidate control owners (who to ping):
- IAM / SSO: Ezra (identity), Lina (onboarding)
- Logging: Keita (infra-logging)
- Deploys / CR: Rohan (platform-eng)
- KMS / secrets: Priya (sec-ops)

Meeting notes template for evidence review (use in quick sync):
- Date: 
- Attendees: 
- Controls reviewed: 
- Artifacts confirmed: 
- Gaps identified: 
- Owner + due date for gap closure: 

Versioning: keep a tiny CHANGELOG at top of evidence bundle: who collected, when, short note. e.g. 2026-02-18 Nora: initial harvest (IAM export + sample PR).

Final thought: this will stay messy for now — capture exact commands and paths so someone else can reproduce. After we have the first full bundle, we can templatize and move things to shared drive under /shared_drives/security-and-compliance/soc2/evidence-bundles/.

References & useful links:
- Confluence page: infra-security SOC2 checklist (linked_artifacts above)
- Jira epic: SEC-4321 (evidence sprint)
- Github: infra repo (PR examples)

Scratch margin notes (one-liners):
- If auditor accepts ephemeral links, provide signed URL with 7-day TTL.
- For DB access proof, prefer query plan + row counts rather than full dump.
- Keep a redaction policy doc handy; saves time during review.

-- Nora
